formalObservation.Composition:
The work is divided visually into three principal zones:

1. Upper-left long-eared figure connected to a sequence of rectangular forms.
2. Upper-right small humanoid figure positioned within an arched enclosure and standing on a rectangular form.
3. Larger long-eared figure occupying the lower portion.

These zones are separated by substantial white space and horizontal structural elements.
formalObservation.Primary Forms:
- Upper-left long-eared figure
- Connected sequence of rectangular units
- Small central humanoid figure
- Arched enclosure
- Large lower long-eared figure
formalObservation.Visible Anatomical Features:
Upper-left figure:

- Large circular eye
- Mouth
- Triangular tooth-like marks
- Two elongated upward projections
- Head/body contour

Upper-right figure:

- Head
- Two eyes
- Mouth
- Hair-like lateral extensions
- Arms
- Torso
- Legs

Lower figure:

- Large oval eye
- Long projecting snout
- Open mouth
- Tongue-like interior form
- Two long upward projections
- Four limb-like extensions
- Two lower supporting legs
formalObservation.Structural Forms:
- Rectangular blocks
- Horizontal connecting line
- Arched frame
- Rectangular pedestal/platform
- Broad rectangular/linear background areas
formalObservation.Repeated Forms:
- Long paired projections
- Rectangular units
- Circular/oval eyes
- Parallel hatching
- Small circular forms beneath rectangular units
formalObservation.Mark-Making:
- broad contour drawing
- parallel hatching
- dense charcoal filling
- light sketch-like lines
- repeated short directional strokes
- localized darker areas
formalObservation.Spatial Strategy:
Segmented / Vignette-like

The three major groups function almost as independent visual episodes within a single page. The term "zones" is used rather than "panels" because there is no clear formal panel structure separating them.
formalObservation.Formal Language:
- Repeated long vertical projections appear across multiple figures.
- Rectangular geometric forms are used as structural supports.
- Organic and geometric construction coexist.
- Figures are reduced into highly legible graphic shapes.
- The composition uses separation and repetition rather than dense overlap.
- The three zones introduce considerable variation while retaining a consistent line vocabulary.
